entry_thesis: The Strait of Hormuz disruption from the US-Israel Iran conflict has removed ~20% of global oil supply, driving WTI toward $80-90+ and pushing energy sector earnings expectations up 8.6% — the only positive S&P 500 sector YTD (+31.8%). The February jobs miss (-92K vs +59K expected) and rising PCE inflation (2.7% Fed projection) confirm stagflation risk, which historically favors energy producers as commodity revenues soar even as broader markets weaken. XLE provides diversified exposure to top US producers (EOG, CVX, COP) beyond the XOM we already hold.
risk: A ceasefire or diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict could cause an abrupt oil price reversal and rapid energy sector sell-off.
catalyst: Ongoing Strait of Hormuz closure and EIA weekly crude inventory data (due March 6) expected to show supply tightness; OPEC+ emergency meeting response to supply disruption.

research_notes.jobs_report: February 2026: -92K jobs vs +59K expected; unemployment 4.4%. Stagflation risk elevated.
research_notes.inflation: CPI +2.4% YoY Feb 2026; Fed projecting PCE 2.7% for 2026 due to oil shock.
research_notes.oil_prices: Brent surpassed $100/b by mid-March; WTI rising sharply in early March as Hormuz closure bites.
research_notes.energy_sector: Only positive S&P 500 sector since Iran war began; up ~31.8% YTD as of early March.
research_notes.thesis_adjustment: Previous GLD recommendation was debunked — gold was falling despite Iran conflict due to $12B ETF outflows. Pivoting back to direct energy play with clear data support. Defense stocks (RTX rec from March 3) also rolling over -8% in March after prior surge. Energy remains the strongest macro signal.
